agentGuide:
WebUI API v2 of qBittorrent. The base URL ends with /api/v2; you then give paths such as /torrents/info. The parameters of a GET go in the query; those of a POST go in body, as an ordinary JSON object — Allkin converts it to the expected form, you need not care.

The useful calls:
· GET /app/version — the version, to check that it answers.
· GET /torrents/info — the list. Filter it: ?filter=downloading|seeding|completed|paused, ?category=…, ?limit=… . The answer is verbose, so use "extract": extract="[].name" or "[state=downloading].name" rather than reading everything.
· GET /torrents/properties?hash=… — the detail of a torrent.
· GET /transfer/info — speeds and totals.
· POST /torrents/add — body {"urls": "<magnet or .torrent URL>", "savepath": "…"}
· POST /torrents/pause and /torrents/resume — body {"hashes": "<hash>|all"}
· POST /torrents/delete — body {"hashes": "…", "deleteFiles": "false"}

A torrent is identified by its "hash" (infohash), which /torrents/info gives in the field hash. Several hashes are separated by "|".

Some calls ask for a human validation: adding, deleting, moving, changing the configuration, shutting down. That is normal, it is not a refusal — say what you are about to do, the user accepts, and the call goes again. Do not try to get around it by another route: there is none.
